sections.label: Land Transport Enforcement Measures Bill
sections.summary: The LTEM Bill amends seven land transport Acts and has five main components, including a PMD registration regime.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: The Land Transport (Enforcement Measures) Bill (LTEM Bill), therefore, amends seven different land transport-related Acts to strengthen LTA's enforcement capacity and enhance safety on our public paths and roads.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: These seven Acts are: (a) the Active Mobility Act (AMA), (b) the Bus Services Industry Act (BSIA), (c) the Land Transport Authority of Singapore Act (LTA Act), (d) the Parking Places Act (PPA), (e) the Rapid Transit Systems Act (RTSA), (f) the Road Traffic Act (RTA), and (g) the Street Works Act (SWA).

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: This Bill has five main components: the first enhances our laws to improve active mobility safety, including introducing a personal mobility device (PMD) registration regime; the second augments LTA's enforcement capacity by empowering outsourced enforcement officers to exercise certain powers of LTA officers, in particular, for certain active mobility offences; the third increases the penalties for persons who cause damage to public streets; the fourth facilitates LTA's efforts to serve notices electronically; and lastly, the Bill makes miscellaneous amendments to update provisions in the various Acts.

sections.label: LTA enforcement offences detected
sections.summary: LTA stepped up enforcement since last year and detected over 1,300 offences since May 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: To address this, LTA has stepped up its enforcement efforts since last year and has detected over 1,300 offences since May 2018.

sections.label: PMD registration regime framework
sections.summary: Clause 11 introduces a new Part 3A to the AMA with sections 28A to 28G for a PMD registration regime.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Clause 11 of the Bill thus introduces a new Part 3A to the AMA, consisting of new sections 28A to 28G, which lay out the legislative framework for a PMD registration regime.

sections.label: Motorised PMA speed limit
sections.summary: AMAP's recommendation to impose a maximum device speed limit of 10 km/h on motorised PMAs was accepted.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: This problem will likely worsen if left unchecked.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: We have, therefore, accepted AMAP's recommendation to impose a maximum device speed limit of 10 kilometres per hour (km/h) on motorised PMAs.

sections.label: UL2272 standard for motorised PMDs
sections.summary: Motorised PMDs on public paths must meet the UL2272 standard, with sale, use and compliance deadlines set.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: For public safety, we intend to require all motorised PMDs intended for use on public paths to conform to the UL2272 standard.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: We intend to prohibit retailers from selling motorised PMDs which are not UL2272-compliant from July 2019 onwards.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Existing owners of motorised PMDs which are not UL2272-compliant can continue to use their devices until end-2020.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: The use of motorised PMDs that are not UL2272-compliant on public paths will be illegal from January 2021 onwards.

sections.label: Penalties for causing damage
sections.summary: Reckless or negligent damage conduct carries up to $50,000 and/or six months, and the maximum fine for intentional damage rises to $100,000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: First, it will be an offence to recklessly or negligently engage in conduct causing damage, with a penalty of up to $50,000 and/or imprisonment up to six months.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Second, the maximum fine for intentionally engaging in conduct causing damage is correspondingly increased from $10,000 to $100,000.

sections.label: Electronic notices for land transport
sections.summary: The Bill amends land-transport Acts so LTA can serve notices electronically instead of only by hardcopy letters.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: In line with our Smart Nation and Digital Government strategies, the Bill amends the various land-transport Acts to allow LTA to serve notices through electronic means, instead of solely through hardcopy letters.

sections.label: Expanding VRLS scope
sections.summary: New sections 43 and 43A of the LTA Act expand VRLS to cover applications, documents and notices under all LTA-administered land transport legislation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: New sections 43 and 43A of the LTA Act will expand the scope of VRLS to cover applications, documents and notices under all land transport legislation administered by LTA.

sections.label: Ang Mo Kio cycling and Silver Zones
sections.summary: Ang Mo Kio Town will add cyclist and PMD lanes, signage, footpaths and parking, and roads around two markets will become Silver Zones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In this regard, I am pleased that at least in Ang Mo Kio Town, we have received support from the Ministry of National Development to improve our town.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We will be adding more dedicated lanes for cyclists and PMD users.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We will be able to install clearer and standardised signages, expand existing footpaths as well as cater for more parking facilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In this year’s Committee of Supply (COS) debate, I also asked the Ministry of Transport (MOT) to speed up the Silver Zone implementation so that more estates with elderly residents can have additional traffic-calming measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am glad that the roads around the two markets in my constituency will soon be revamped to be Silver Zones.

sections.label: PMD insurance not mandatory
sections.summary: PMD users are not required to buy insurance, though a local firm launched a plan in 2016 covering deaths, disabilities, medical expenses and third-party liabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Earlier, the Senior Minister of State spoke about the increased number of people who were involved in accidents whereby users of PMDs, electric-bikes and so on were the main cause of accidents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It is currently not mandatory for PMD users to buy insurance although, back in 2016, a local insurance firm launched a first-of-its-kind insurance plan that covered accidental deaths, permanent disabilities, medical expenses against injuries and third-party liabilities for that accident when riding, mounting or dismounting a bicycle or PMD.

sections.label: Registering e-bikes and PMDs
sections.summary: Electric bikes, known as PABs, must be registered with number plates, and the Bill now requires PMD ownership to be registered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Last year, electric bikes, otherwise known in our statutes as PABs, are required to be registered and every legal e-bike must have a number plate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Today, we are asked to pass a Bill requiring ownership of PMDs to be registered.

sections.label: Rejected PMD age restriction
sections.summary: The member filed a Parliamentary Question, but MOT rejected the suggestion to restrict PMD use to those aged 18 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Two months ago, I filed a Parliamentary Question on this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But MOT has rejected my suggestion for the use of PMDs to be restricted to those who are 18 and above.

sections.label: AMAP speed limit recommendation
sections.summary: AMAP has recommended reducing the speed limit for bicycles and PMDs on footpaths from 15 km/h to 10 km/h.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: AMAP has recommended to reduce the speed limit for bicycles and PMDs on footpaths from 15 km/h to 10 km/h.

sections.label: Parliamentary Question on bicycle handlebars
sections.summary: The MP asked the Minister for Transport about awareness of the 700 mm handlebar width limit and whether owners get a chance to change handlebars before impoundment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Last month, I filed a Parliamentary Question (PQ) to the Minister for Transport asking whether any action is taken to ensure that owners of bicycles with handlebars exceeding 700 millimetres (mm) length are made aware that such bicycles are not allowed on footpaths and walkways, and whether owners are given reasonable opportunity to change the handlebars without their bicycles being impounded immediately when they are found on footpaths or walkways.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In the answer to my PQ, Minister Khaw Boon Wan said, amongst other things, that the width limit of 700 mm has been widely publicised by LTA since 2016 through numerous platforms, including videos, posters, banners, and that LTA also works with retailers, interest groups and active mobility patrol volunteers to reach out to the public about this width limit.

sections.label: Parliament debates on PMD regulation
sections.summary: Over two and a half years Parliament debated regulating PMDs, electric bikes and bicycles, and shared footpath use; the AMA passed in January 2017 and came into force this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin): Mr Speaker, in the past two and a half years, there has been various debates in Parliament on the issue of the regulation of PMDs, electric bikes and other bicycles, as well as the introduction of shared use of footpaths by bicycles and PMDs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We passed the AMA in January 2017 which came into force earlier this year.

sections.label: Debate on mandatory PMD registration
sections.summary: The debate concerns whether registration should be mandatory for PMD owners, and an elderly man said the cycling regime feels less safe than before.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Today, what we are debating is whether we should make registration mandatory for PMD owners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Earlier this year, an elderly man told me that he feels that the cycling regime is not as safe as before.

sections.label: Public education for riders
sections.summary: The passage asks whether public education covers riders of all ages and notes safe riding courses run by LTA and the Singapore Road Safety Council.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Is the current scope of public education enough to cover riders of all ages?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We now run some public education courses, such as the safe riding courses organised by LTA and Singapore Road Safety Council.

sections.label: Elderly fear PMD accidents
sections.summary: Many elderly people are terrified of getting into accidents with PMDs while walking along void decks or walkways.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Many elderly people are terrified of getting into accidents with PMDs while they are walking along the void decks or walkways.

sections.label: Support for the Bill
sections.summary: The Member states that despite concerns raised, he supports the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: (In English): Mr Speaker, notwithstanding the concerns that I have raised, I support this Bill.

sections.label: Heavier penalties for reckless riders
sections.summary: The Member seeks heavier penalties, a possible ban, and asks about liability insurance and PMD registration for compensation.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We should have heavier penalties for offenders who ride recklessly and cause serious injury to the victims.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I do not think the proposed fine of $2,000, or imprisonment for a term not exceeding three months, or to both, under section 28(3) is adequate.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The penalties must have a stronger bite to wake up the would-be offenders.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Also, I would like to ask whether the Minister will consider imposing a ban on those who cause the victims to suffer serious debilitating permanent injury or death.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Given that accidents involving e-scooters or PMDs can cause serious injuries to pedestrians, what is the reason for the delay in the implementation of liability insurance?

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: How can the registration of PMDs help the victims in accidents in the claim for compensation?

sections.label: Deterrence and PMD rider checks
sections.summary: The Member questions whether the $2,000 fine deters, seeks a phone ban, and notes pillion riders and rider checks.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For example, is the current fine of $2,000 enough to deter dangerous behaviours?

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Using handphones on a PMD should be treated the same as using phones while driving and should be banned.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Allowing a pillion rider on the PMD will cause higher impact on pedestrians in an accident.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In addition, the health condition and age of the PMD rider, and how well the PMD is being maintained, are areas that the Government is not checking regularly.

sections.label: Bill related to AMA
sections.summary: The Member notes that a large part of the Bill relates to AMA, which came into force earlier this year.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Most notably, a large part of this Bill is related to AMA, which only came into force earlier this year.

sections.label: Rising enforcement costs
sections.summary: The Member states that enforcement costs, including outsourced policing, will rise as rules become more intricate.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: At the same time, the cost of enforcement, including the outsourcing of the policing work, is going to rise, as the rules are made more intricate.

sections.label: Concerns on costs and benefits
sections.summary: The Member asks whether costs and benefits were analysed, road users studied, and the changes desirable.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With this in mind, Sir, what I am concerned about is whether there has been a clear analysis of the costs and benefits involved, whether there is any reliable study into how the majority of road users have been impacted, and whether these changes are desirable.

sections.label: PMD pillion safety question
sections.summary: The Minister clarified pillion riders are not prohibited, but safety and effects on other road users cannot be separated from how PMDs are used.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Although the Minister already clarified that the carrying of pillion riders is not prohibited under current regulations, the question as to whether it is safe for PMDs to be used to carry pillions and how it affects other road users, especially elderly and vulnerable pedestrians, cannot be dissociated from the way PMDs are currently being used.

sections.label: Reported PMD accident cases
sections.summary: A Straits Times report cited 19 reported accidents involving PMDs, bicycles or electric bikes on public paths, rising to 42 in 2016 and 128 last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In a report by The Straits Times, there were 19 reported cases of accidents involving PMDs, bicycles or electric bikes on public paths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In 2016, the figure increased to 42 and went up to 128 last year.

sections.label: Personal liability insurance for PMDs
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to consider mandating personal liability insurance tied to PMD registration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Just like my parliamentary colleague, hon Er Dr Lee Bee Wah, I would like to urge the Government to consider mandating users to possess a personal liability insurance which would be tied to the registration of their PMD.

sections.label: Scepticism over PMD speed limit
sections.summary: Proposals to cut the footpath speed limit from 15 km/hr to 10 km/hr face scepticism over enforcement and users' ability to gauge speed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Even with the recent proposals to cut speed limit of PMD users using footpath from 15 km/hr to 10 km/hr, there has been a lot of scepticism on its effectiveness due to challenges in enforcement and the difficulty for an average PMD user to be able to gauge its speed.

sections.label: Support for PMD amendments
sections.summary: The speaker supports the amendments based on extensive consultations and seeks clarifications on the scope and implementation of the PMD registration requirement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am thus supportive of these amendments, which are based on extensive consultations, and I have just a number of clarifications to make.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I have some clarifications on the scope and implementation of the PMD registration requirement under the new Part 3A.

sections.label: Enforcement powers and vehicle disposal
sections.summary: Enforcement powers under several sections are extended to outsourced officers, and clause 27 removes the requirement to make reasonable inquiry before disposing a vehicle.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Next, enforcement powers under sections 41, 44, 45, 46, 47, 48 and 50 have been extended to outsourced enforcement officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Next, clause 27 amends the current section 53(2) of AMA to remove the requirement to make reasonable inquiry to locate the owner of a vehicle before disposing it.

sections.label: Footpath width and mobility devices
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry is reviewing minimum footpath widths given mobility devices up to 0.7 metres wide, and describes the Bill's amendments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Given that mobility devices are now permitted up to a width of 0.7 metres, this leaves barely enough space when two mobility devices pass each other on a footpath that is 1.5 metre wide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Thus, beyond these amendments, is the Ministry reviewing the minimum width of existing and new footpaths?

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In general, the amendments in the first part of the Bill aimed to expand the restrictions to include mobility vehicles and motorised wheelchair, ban on all shared paths and footpath, increase accountability through registration and empower outsourced enforcement.

sections.label: Minimum registration age review
sections.summary: The passage states that the minimum age for registration under section 67(2) in clause 34 should be thoroughly reviewed with evidence-based data.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On the amendments in section 67(2) in clause 34, the minimum age for a person to be registered should be thoroughly reviewed in tandem with evidence-based data.

sections.label: Ban impact on PMD users
sections.summary: The passage questions the impact of banning PMDs on shared paths and footpaths on people who rely on them to commute or work.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While it is a straightforward solution to ban PMDs on shared paths and footpaths, we should question the impact on people who rely on PMDs to commute to work or use it for work, such as in the case of some food delivery personnel.

sections.label: Incentive scheme for compliance
sections.summary: The passage asks whether an incentive-based scheme rewarding people who conform to rules and have a clean record could be considered.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Moving forward, could we also consider looking towards an incentive-based scheme or system that rewards people who conform to these rules and regulations and have a clean record?

sections.label: Outsourced enforcement officers welcomed
sections.summary: The passage states more enforcement officers are needed due to PMD prevalence and welcomes outsourced enforcement officers introduced in the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Due to the prevalence of PMDs and the wide areas of coverage, we need more enforcement officers on the ground to monitor users and ensure compliance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Hence, I welcome the introduction of outsourced enforcement officers in this Bill, which will be very useful and helpful for the very labour-intensive task of enforcement.

sections.label: Seller compliance and battery testing
sections.summary: The passage asks how LTA will enforce seller compliance including online sales, and whether certification of approved models includes battery safety testing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Hence, I would like to ask how LTA is going to enforce strict compliance from sellers, including online sales, so that only authorised models are imported into Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This Bill will require that all e-scooters are registered and they have to display the registration mark.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Will the process of certification of approved models also include testing of the batteries and their level of safety in view of the number of fires due to e-scooters with substandard batteries?

sections.label: Non-compliant PMDs and countermeasures
sections.summary: The speaker says non-compliant devices should be greatly reduced but asks the Minister for countermeasures since the Government cannot ban all illegal PMDs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As a result, the number of non-compliant ones should be greatly reduced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, I am still worried that the Government cannot ban all illegal PMDs, so I would like to ask the Minister if there is any countermeasure.

sections.label: PMD accidents on public paths
sections.summary: The speaker notes devices reduce walking effort and time, but reports accidents involving PMDs, bicycles or e-bikes rose from 19 in 2015 to 42 in 2016 and 128 in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: For the users, the devices reduce walking effort and time significantly, but the black sheep amongst them have caused injury to pedestrians, many of which go unreported.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I note with alarm the rapid increase in the number of reported accidents involving PMDs, bicycles or e-bikes on public paths from 19 cases in 2015, to 42 in 2016, and 128 in 2017.

sections.label: GPS microchips and e-scooter registration
sections.summary: The speaker suggests GPS microchips to track PMD usage, welcomes compulsory e-scooter registration and higher fire safety standards, and urges more stringent measures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: To ensure that we do not penalise the good riders, we can consider installing microchips with Global Positioning System (GPS) in PMDs so that we have a way of tracking the usage of such devices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I am very pleased that the Bill will make it compulsory for all e-scooters to be registered and higher fire safety standards will be introduced for motorised PMDs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: There have been regular incidents involving e-scooters and many of my residents are very worried that, one day, a neighbour’s PMD will lead to fires which will engulf their homes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: While I urge for even more stringent measures to regulate PMDs, I appreciate the measures taken in the Bill which are steps in the right direction.

sections.label: Mandatory registration of certain PMDs
sections.summary: The mandatory registration of certain PMDs is described as a welcome enhancement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The mandatory registration of certain PMDs is a welcome enhancement.

sections.label: Extending provisions to online sellers
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Ministry would extend the provisions to individual sellers and those who carry out sales online if they are not covered.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: If it does not cover individual sellers and those who carry out sales online, would the Ministry consider extending these provisions to address such sales?

sections.label: 128 PMD accidents in 2017
sections.summary: In 2017, it was reported there were 128 accidents involving PMDs on public paths.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: In 2017, it was reported there were 128 accidents involving PMDs on public paths.

sections.label: Small Claims for Personal Injury
sections.summary: It suggests considering whether personal injury claims below $20,000 can be decided at the Small Claims Tribunal, as filing costs may be prohibitive.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: It is also likely that the claims for personal injury and property damage are likely to be of a small quantum and the current process and cost of filing a civil claim for personal injury could be prohibitive in nature.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: It might be useful to consider if personal injury claims below $20,000 can be decided at the Small Claims Tribunal.

sections.label: Registration and Identification Marks
sections.summary: The proposed registration regime requires all users to affix an identification mark prominently on their device as a first step to penalise errant users.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: The current proposed registration regime requiring all users to affix an identification mark prominently on their device is the first step towards striking down errant users and penalising them for their reckless riding habits and behaviour.

sections.label: Third-Party Liability Insurance for Riders
sections.summary: It states that mandating insurance coverage for users who utilise PMDs as a tool for work is beneficial, as PMD incidents can be fatal or cause serious injuries.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: For example, they should provide third-party liability insurance for their riders.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: We know that incidents caused by PMDs can be fatal or cause very serious injuries.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Therefore, mandating some form of insurance coverage for users who utilise PMDs as a tool for work is beneficial for all stakeholders.

sections.label: Enforcement Against Errant PMD Users
sections.summary: It states that more enforcement is needed to curb errant PMD users and improve footpath safety, citing frequent PMD-related fires including one in the speaker's ward.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: But the current state of affairs is such that more enforcement is needed to curb errant PMD users and improve the safety of our footpaths.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: We have seen frequent cases of PMD-related fires and there was such a fire case in my ward just last month.

sections.label: Amendments for PMD Enforcement
sections.summary: It states that amendments to laws are timely to tighten enforcement and safeguard public interest amid PMD growth and bicycle sharing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: With the increase in disamenities arising from the explosive growth of PMDs and the introduction of bicycle sharing into our land transport landscape, it is timely that we make the necessary amendments to our laws to tighten enforcement and safeguard public interest.

sections.label: PMD Users Stopping at Crossings
sections.summary: It welcomes the Ministry's acceptance of AMAP's recommendations requiring cyclists and PMD users to stop at road crossings, noting 80% of PMD accidents from 2016 to 2018 involved vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: On the topic of PMDs, I note that the Ministry has recently accepted AMAP’s recommendations to require cyclists and PMD users to stop at road crossings and look out for vehicles before resuming their journeys.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I welcome this move, as between 2016 and 2018, 80% of accidents involving PMDs were due to PMD collisions with vehicles.

sections.label: Blocking online sale of non-compliant PMDs
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Ministry to block online sales of non-compliant PMDs, citing fires from charging batteries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We have already seen an increasing number of cases where PMDs, presumably non-compliant ones, had caught fire when their batteries were being charged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I urge the Ministry to put in place measures to block the online sale of such non-compliant PMDs.

sections.label: Increasing maximum fine for intentional damage
sections.summary: The speaker supports raising the maximum fine for intentionally causing significant damage from $10,000 to $100,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Besides the large repair bill, there is significant impact to work productivity and economic opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I, therefore, support the Bill's proposal to increase the maximum fine for intentionally causing significant damage, from $10,000 today to $100,000.

sections.label: Mandatory training for PMD users
sections.summary: The speaker says mandatory training for PMD users would help ensure safety remains a key priority.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Educating our growing number of PMD users through some form of mandatory training would also go a long way in ensuring that safety remains a key priority even as the PMD users are scooting about Singapore.

sections.label: AMAP path-sharing safety recommendations
sections.summary: The passage states AMAP recommendations were accepted, including e-scooter registration, a 10 km/h PMA speed limit, helmets on roads, and stop-and-look at crossings.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: We recently accepted AMAP's recommendations to further improve the safety of path-sharing.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: This includes mandating the registration of e-scooters, implementing a device speed limit of 10 km/h on personal mobility aids (PMAs), mandating helmets for active mobility device users on roads, and mandating "stop and look" at traffic crossings.

sections.label: Penalties for reckless riding under AMA
sections.summary: Under AMA, individuals who ride recklessly can face fines up to $5,000 and up to six months' imprisonment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Under AMA, individuals who ride recklessly can face up to $5,000 in fines and up to six months' imprisonment.

sections.label: LTA enforcement and detected offences
sections.summary: With enhanced AMA enforcement powers since May 2018, LTA detected over 1,300 active mobility offences between 1 May and 15 August 2018.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: With enhanced enforcement powers under the AMA since May 2018, LTA has stepped up its enforcement efforts and has detected over 1,300 active mobility offences between 1 May and 15 August 2018.

sections.label: Enforcement against errant PMD retailers
sections.summary: LTA seized 18 PMDs and two PABs from 18 retailers for non-compliance and will keep enforcing against errant retailers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: LTA recently conducted an enforcement blitz against 18 retailers and seized a total of 18 PMDs and two PABs for non-compliance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: We agree with Er Dr Lee Bee Wah on the need to continue to enforce against such errant retailers and will continue to take a strong enforcement stance towards them.

sections.label: Non-compliant devices registration and confiscation
sections.summary: Non-compliant devices cannot be registered, and those used on public paths will be confiscated.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Non-compliant devices will not be allowed to be registered, and those used on public paths will be confiscated.

sections.label: New footpath width requirement
sections.summary: New footpaths without adjacent cycling paths will be 1.8 metres wide, up from the previous 1.5 metres minimum.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: New footpaths with no adjacent cycling paths will now be 1.8 metres wide, wider than the previous minimum width of 1.5 metres.

sections.label: Mandatory SRP for reckless riders
sections.summary: Reckless riders must attend the SRP before they may compound their offence, as education on safe riding is preferred.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Instead, it is better to educate them on safe riding behaviours.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: This is why we have made it mandatory for reckless riders to attend the SRP before they may compound their offence.

sections.label: PMA and PMD road use and UL2272
sections.summary: PMA or PMD users may ride on roads only as far as needed to avoid obstructions, and UL2272 compliance will be required.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Mr Dennis Tan also asked about whether PMA users would be allowed on roads if the footpaths are obstructed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: It is not an offence for PMA or PMD users to ride on roads in such a situation, but they should travel along the road only for the distance necessary to avoid the obstruction.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: As earlier mentioned, we intend to require all motorised PMDs used on public paths to conform to the UL2272 standard.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: We intend to prohibit the sale of devices that do not comply with UL2272 from July 2019, and use of these devices on public paths from January 2021.

sections.label: Fine increase and suing for repairs
sections.summary: The fine for intentionally causing damage rises from $10,000 to $100,000, and LTA may sue for full repair costs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Apart from raising the fine for intentionally engaging in conduct causing damage from $10,000 to $100,000, LTA also retains the option of suing for the full cost of repairs.

sections.label: Compensation avenues for accident victims
sections.summary: There are currently three ways for accident victims to seek compensation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: On her first question on compensation avenues, currently there are three ways where the victim of accidents can seek compensation.

sections.label: Town Council by-laws and AMA
sections.summary: AMA applies to all public paths including Town Council areas, so Town Councils cannot ban PMDs or enforce differing by-laws.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: On the second question on the Town Council by-laws, AMA applies to all public paths, including paths in Town Council areas.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Therefore, Town Councils are not allowed to ban PMDs on paths or enforce any by-laws that differ from the provisions in AMA.

sections.label: Encouraging PMD third-party insurance
sections.summary: LTA and MOT grapple with these issues, and one way to address them is encouraging PMD users to buy third-party liability insurance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Indeed, these are issues that LTA, together with MOT, do grapple with to see how we can best address them and, of course, one of the ways to address this issue is to encourage PMD users to purchase third-party liability insurance.
